<subject>Re: AgroTrade India From Bharat Commodities</subject>
<body>
Reyansh Salvi

My understanding is that Hebert doesn't have the legal authority (and the filing never makes clear) to suspend procurement under the Purchase Agreement (he probably doesn't have the political support for this either).

AgroTrade, however, could support this in its filing as a method to help move the farmer contract issue forward.

Hardik





	Reyansh Krish
	Sent by: Reyansh Krish
	3/19/2024 10:04 AM
		 
		 To: Dakshesh Basak, Libni Kibe, Charita 
Balay, Amruta Wali, Manya 
Bal, Hardik Pal, Christopher 
Baral, Matthew Nazareth, Vrinda Mangat
		 cc: 
		 Subject: AgroTrade India From Bharat Commodities

FYI.  Any thoughts Dakshesh & Co.? Is release from contracts an "increase supply" option?  My fear is that QF farms get released and then Maharashtra's "police state" mentality kicks in, enacting local farm regulations, etc. to ensure that the crop from the QF farms stays in Maharashtra.

Best,
Reyansh
</body>
